title: Parallel QEC Decoding Applied to Distributed Quantum Computing
authors: Gabriele Incardona, Davide Ferrari, Michele Amoretti
abstract: A novel parallel approach is proposed for QEC decoding based on Belief Propagation with Ordered Statistics Decoding. The main idea is to pre-process the error vectors obtained from Belief Propagation by applying Singular Value Decomposition locally to sub-regions of the lattice. The proposed approach is applied to distributed quantum computers and evaluated in terms of complexity, accuracy, and scalability.
summary: This paper proposes a novel parallel decoding strategy for QEC in distributed quantum computers by integrating Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) locally into the Belief Propagation and Ordered Statistics Decoding pipeline. The method significantly reduces computational complexity while maintaining high logical accuracy, proving that local compression is effective where global compression fails.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing efficient, scalable decoding algorithms for Quantum Error Correction (QEC) when implemented on distributed quantum computing hardware.
main_result: Applying Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) as a *local* preprocessing filter significantly improves the computational complexity and maintains high logical accuracy compared to global or non-optimized decoding methods.
method: The approach combines Belief Propagation (BP) for initial error estimation with Ordered Statistics Decoding (OSD), introducing SVD locally on sub-regions of the lattice to compress the error vector basis before final decoding.
model_or_system: The work models quantum computation using stabilizer codes, specifically focusing on Surface Codes implemented across a distributed network of Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) connected by quantum links.
key_observables: Logical Accuracy (%) over 1000 trials; Computational Complexity ($O(m^3 + (n/r)^3)$); Execution Time (seconds).
important_parameters: SVD Energy Threshold ($\epsilon$); Physical Error Rate ($	ext{perr}$); Number of QPUs ($\#$ QPU); Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that local SVD compression retains sufficient topological information for accurate decoding, unlike global compression which fails due to loss of inter-qubit correlations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the planar code structure and circuits for syndrome extraction. Comparisons show performance vs. energy threshold (Table 2) and scalability vs. number of QPUs (Table 3).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces QEC decoding bottlenecks using BP/OSD on surface codes. It then proposes the novel local SVD pre-processing step, analyzes its complexity gains over centralized methods, and finally validates performance and scalability across varying error rates and node counts.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation, the techniques of dimensionality reduction via SVD applied to structured matrices (like parity checks) are relevant for analyzing complex correlation structures in many-body systems or simulating highly entangled states.
